subject: physics

items.q: What happens to energy when a device runs?
items.correct: It is transferred and dissipated (often as heat); never destroyed.
items.misconception: It is used up and ceases to exist.
items.random_wrong: It is created from nothing by the device.
items.why: Conservation of energy: total energy is constant; wasted energy spreads to the surroundings.

items.q: Does 'renewable' mean an energy resource causes no harm?
items.correct: No — it means it won't run out; it may still have some impact.
items.misconception: Yes, renewables cause no environmental harm at all.
items.random_wrong: It just means it is the cheapest option.
items.why: Renewable refers to replenishment, not zero impact (e.g. biofuels release CO₂).

items.q: How are power and energy different?
items.correct: Power is the rate of energy transfer (watts); energy is the total (joules).
items.random_wrong: Power equals energy multiplied by time.
items.why: Power = energy ÷ time; a higher-power device transfers energy faster.
